**Overview.** A/T/G/C = 758/806/735/701, overall GC 47.9%. No BLAST/database access from this environment, so everything below is from intrinsic sequence statistics.

- **ORF structure:** ATG at 1161–1163 → TAA at 2175–2177; 1,017 nt, 338 codons. No alternative in-frame start (preceding in-frame stop sits at 1149–1151).
- **Stop-codon suppression:** the gene's frame is stop-free for 1,023 nt (1152–2174) — only 1 in-frame stop in 342 codons vs ~19 expected from local base composition. A null model (3,000 backgrounds matched for composition *and* dinucleotide statistics) never produced an ATG→stop ORF this long (99.9th percentile = 672 nt, max 846 nt).
- **Codon-position bias (classic CDS signature):** GC1 = 55.8% / GC2 = 37.5% / GC3 = 70.8% — silent sites strongly GC-skewed. This skew holds window-by-window across 1200–2100 in this frame and in no other frame, on either strand.
- **Composition island:** the ORF (GC 54.7%) sits in a ~1-kb GC-rich segment (~1200–2100; 51–58% GC in 200-bp windows) against AT-rich flanks (left 1–1150: 43.9%; right 2178–3000: 45.2%).
- **Synonymous usage** deviates far more from composition expectation than any window of the flanking DNA (χ² ≈ 262, df ≈ 61, vs ≤103 anywhere in background; e.g. Leu = 21×CTG vs 2×TTA).

**Product (predicted):** 338 aa, ~37.9 kDa, basic (18% K/R/H vs 11% D/E, charge rising to +21/−13 in the C-terminal third), no transmembrane helix (max 19-aa hydropathy 1.09), no convincing signal peptide, no recognizable catalytic motifs (P-loop, Rossmann, HExxH, zinc-finger, etc. all absent). Likely a soluble, basic protein; no functional call possible without homology search. Translation saved to `scratch/orf_translations.fasta`.

**Regulatory context is conspicuously absent:** no AGGAGG-like Shine–Dalgarno within 30 nt of the start (best partial match 4/6 at 1127–1132), no convincing −35/−10 promoter, and no GC-stem + T-tract terminator after the stop (nearest T-run, 2360–2364, has no stem). It reads like a bare CDS without its native flanking signals.

## 2. Ambiguous long ORF — minus strand, 235–953

The reverse strand holds an ATG→TGA ORF: 238 aa, 717 nt (ATG at plus-coords 951–953, stop at 235–237), with a textbook RBS: **GGAGG on the minus strand (= CCTCC at 958–962), ending exactly 4 nt upstream of the ATG**. Its length is not explainable as chance (0/2,000 shuffled versions of the surrounding background reach 717 nt; max 666).

However, it fails every test that identifies feature 1 as real: no codon-position bias (GC1 = GC2 = 47.1%, GC3 = 36.6% — GC3 is ~7 points *below* the local background, the opposite of real-gene behavior), codon usage uncorrelated with the plus-strand gene (r = 0.06), and Leu usage is generic AT-bias (7×TTA). I'd treat it as a **putative ORF of uncertain status — possibly a decoy** — the top follow-up candidate for a BLAST/annotation check.

## 3. Checked and negative

- No CRISPR arrays, no spacer-repeat periodicity; no tandem repeats beyond trivial runs (longest: CAG×3 at 2662–2670); homopolymers only up to 6 nt (e.g. GGGGGG at 105–110, TTTTTT at 281–286, 443–448, 2898–2903).

**Bottom line:** the notable feature is a single well-supported ~1-kb gene (plus strand, 1161–2177, 338 aa) of unknown function, embedded in otherwise featureless AT-rich DNA; the flagged RBS-associated 238-aa reverse-strand ORF (235–953) is the one thing I'd verify against a database.
